# 'md_exec' Dialect

_How the MD computation is organized._

The `md_exec` dialect expresses loops over particles and over the pairs
of a physical neighbor structure, and the construction of such
structures. It says over which set a kernel runs and how the kernel
accesses fields: which it reads, which it accumulates into, and which
global sums it contributes to.

In the value form, which is the form defined here, the ops take and
return field values.

Discardable attributes of the storage form (D337, `StorageSet.h`):

- `md_exec.tuple_set` on the builder of an incidence buffer and on its
  tuple loops declares the tuple set of the buffer, which its type does
  not carry yet.
- `md_exec.typed_storage` on a module marks storage that
  `md-exec-assign-storage` assigned, whose loop operands must be tagged
  with their set; the conversions to loops and to a device remove both.
- `md_exec.input_set_boundary` is a unit marker on `memref.cast` where
  an external plain input first acquires its declared storage set. The
  dialect verifies its placement, value, and set provenance
  (D345).


## Operations

### `md_exec.build_cells` (::mdir::md_exec::BuildCellsOp)

_Bins particles into cells_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.build_cells` $positions `,` $cell `width` `(` $width `)` attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($positions)) `->` qualified(type($result))
```

Divides the simulation cell into cells that are at least `width` wide in
every direction and assigns each particle to one.

```mlir
%cells = md_exec.build_cells %x, %cell width(2.8)
           : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64> -> !mdrt.cells<@atoms>
```

Traits: `AlwaysSpeculatableImplTrait`

Interfaces: `ConditionallySpeculatable`, `NoMemoryEffect (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{}`

### `md_exec.build_edges` (::mdir::md_exec::BuildEdgesOp)

_Finds the pairs of images within a cutoff_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.build_edges` $neighbors `,` $positions `,` $cell `cutoff` `(` $cutoff `)` attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($neighbors)) `,` qualified(type($positions))
              `->` type($results)
```

The pairs of `md.edges` at the positions `positions` in the cell
`cell` (D277, docs/metatomic-ml1.md, Section 12):
for each particle `i`, every image `s` of each particle `j` of its row
in `neighbors`, and of `i` itself, with `|x_j − x_i + s H| < cutoff`.

```mlir
%e = md_exec.build_edges %nl, %x, %cell cutoff(0.7)
       : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
         -> !md.edges<@atoms>
```

The structure must be a matrix: its rows hold every neighbor of a
particle, by its nearest image. Each build of the structure gives each
particle `i` slots for its candidates, the images within the reach of
the structure at the positions of the build, `C_i` of them at the
offsets `O_i`; the op writes into the slots of `i` the candidates
within `cutoff` at `positions` first, then the others, and counts the
first. A candidate within the cutoff now was within the reach at the
build while the structure is valid, so every pair of `md.edges` has a
slot.

In the storage form the op takes the buffer of the positions and
returns, on the device, the slots, one row `(i, j, s_a, s_b, s_c)` for
each, in the order of `i`; the number of pairs within the cutoff of each
particle; the offsets `O_i`, one more than the particles; and, on the
host, the number that the runtime gave the last build of the slots,
which no other build in the process has, so that a reader can tell
where the slots and the offsets changed. The buffers are those of the
structure: a build replaces what they hold.

```mlir
%slots, %counts, %offsets, %builds = md_exec.build_edges %nl, %x, %cell
    cutoff(0.7) : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, memref<?x3xf64, 1>
    -> memref<?x5xi32, 1>, memref<?xi32, 1>, memref<?xi32, 1>, i64
```

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

</table>

### `md_exec.build_incidence` (::mdir::md_exec::BuildIncidenceOp)

_Finds, for every particle, the tuples it is a member of_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.build_incidence` $relation (`size` `(` $size^ `)`)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($relation)) `->` qualified(type($result))
```

A loop over tuples visits, for every particle, the tuples that the
particle is a member of. This op finds them.

```mlir
%incidence = md_exec.build_incidence %angles
    : !md.relation<@atoms, 3, reversal, @angles>
      -> !mdrt.incidence<@atoms, 3, @angles>
```

The members of a tuple are places in the fields of the particles. The
result holds as long as the particles keep their places.

In the storage form the op takes the buffer of the members and the
number of particles, and it returns a new buffer of ragged rows
(compressed sparse rows), one row for each particle. For $N$ particles
and $M$ memberships (the number of tuples times the arity $a$), each
an entry of $E = a + 2$ values, the buffer holds $N + 2 + E(M + 1)$
elements:

| Elements | Hold |
|---|---|
| `[0]` | $N$ |
| `[1, N + 2)` | the offsets $o_0 = 0 \le \dots \le o_N = M$, in entries |
| `[N + 2 + E j, N + 2 + E (j + 1))` | entry $j$: the number of the tuple, the place of the particle in it, and its members |
| the last $E$ | an entry of zeros |

The row of particle $i$ is the entries $o_i$ to $o_{i+1}$, its tuples
in ascending order of their numbers (and of the place, for a particle
at two places of one tuple). Code reads a row through one accessor
(`include/mdir/Conversion/RaggedRows.h`).

```mlir
%incidence = md_exec.build_incidence %members size(%n)
    : memref<?x3xi32> -> memref<?xi32>
```

The buffer of the members is on the host. The result is where its type
says: on the host, or on a device.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `relation` | A set of tuples of distinct particles or buffer of the members of tuples |
| `size` | index |

#### Results:

| Result | Description |
| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | For every particle, the tuples that it is a member of or buffer of the tuples of each particle |



### `md_exec.build_neighbors` (::mdir::md_exec::BuildNeighborsOp)

_Builds a physical neighbor structure_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.build_neighbors` $cells `,` $positions `,` $cell (`centers` `(` $centers^ `)`)?
              `cutoff` `(` $cutoff `)` `skin` `(` $skin `)`
              `kind` `(` $kind `)` `width` `(` $width `)`
              (`images` `(` $images^ `)`)?
              (`exclude` `(` $excluded^ `:` qualified(type($excluded)) `)`)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($cells)) `,` qualified(type($positions))
              `->` qualified(type($result))
```

The structure is built at the configuration `positions` with the
extended cutoff `cutoff + skin`. It holds the directed list

```text
L = { (i, j) : i ≠ j, r_ij < cutoff + skin }
```

and is valid for any configuration in which no particle has moved more
than `skin / 2` and the cell is unchanged.

`width` is the number of neighbors that the structure can hold for one
particle.

```mlir
%nl = md_exec.build_neighbors %cells, %x, %cell
        cutoff(2.5) skin(0.3) kind(matrix) width(96)
        : !mdrt.cells<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
        -> !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>
```

With `exclude`, the structure leaves out the pairs of an incidence
structure of a tuple set of arity 2. `width` is the room a row has at
first, for the neighbors of a particle before those are left out; a
build that finds a row too narrow makes the rows wider.

With `centers(%n)`, the first `n` particles of the set are the centers:
the structure has the rows of the centers, whose entries are any
particles of the set, and a loop over it takes those rows only. With
`images(explicit)`, the positions carry their images, as the owned and
ghost rows of a domain do (D290, docs/distributed-ml2.md,
Section 7.2): the structure holds every pair within `cutoff + skin` in
the plain difference of the positions, and may hold more, which the
cutoff of a loop removes. Such a structure is a matrix.

```mlir
%nl = md_exec.build_neighbors %cells, %x, %cell centers(%n)
        cutoff(2.0) skin(0.0) kind(matrix) width(64) images(explicit)
        : !mdrt.cells<@dd.d0.local>, !md.field<@dd.d0.local, 3 x f64>
        -> !mdrt.neighbors<@dd.d0.local>
```

Traits: `AlwaysSpeculatableImplTrait`, `AttrSizedOperandSegments`

Interfaces: `ConditionallySpeculatable`, `NoMemoryEffect (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

### `md_exec.build_triplets` (::mdir::md_exec::BuildTripletsOp)

_Finds the triplets centered on each particle_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.build_triplets` $neighbors `,` $positions `,` $cell `cutoff` `(` $cutoff `)` attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($neighbors)) `,` qualified(type($positions))
              `->` qualified(type($result))
```

The triplets of `md.triplets` at the positions `positions`: for each
particle `i`, each unordered pair `{j, k}` of the particles of its row
in `neighbors` with `r_ij < cutoff` and `r_ik < cutoff` once, as the
tuple `(j, i, k)`, `j` before `k` in the row.

```mlir
%t = md_exec.build_triplets %nl, %x, %cell cutoff(0.43065)
       : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
         -> !md.relation<@atoms, 3, reversal>
```

The structure must be a matrix: its rows hold every neighbor of a
particle. The result is a relation without a tuple set; its incidence
structure is built by `md_exec.build_incidence`.

In the storage form the op takes the buffer of the positions and
returns a new buffer of the members on the host, one row for each
triplet, as many rows as there are triplets (D160).

```mlir
%members = md_exec.build_triplets %nl, %x, %cell cutoff(0.43065)
             : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, memref<?x3xf64>
               -> memref<?x3xi32>
```

_The diagonal and the tilts of a cell_

Syntax:

### `md_exec.empty_neighbors` (::mdir::md_exec::EmptyNeighborsOp)

_A neighbor structure that is valid for no configuration_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.empty_neighbors` (`size` `(` $size^ `)` `positions` `(` $positions `)`)?
              `kind` `(` $kind `)` `width` `(` $width `)`
              (`exclude` `(` $excluded^ `:` qualified(type($excluded)) `)`)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($result))
```

The first refresh of the structure builds it.

```mlir
%nl0 = md_exec.empty_neighbors kind(matrix) width(96)
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>
```

In the storage form the op allocates the storage of a structure for
`size` particles. `positions` is the type of the buffers that hold the
positions the structure is built at. The storage is where those buffers
are: on the host, or on a device if the type has a memory space.

```mlir
%nl = md_exec.empty_neighbors size(%n) positions(memref<?x3xf32>)
        kind(matrix) width(96) : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>
```

`exclude` is as for `md_exec.build_neighbors`: every build of the
structure leaves out those pairs.

### `md_exec.join` (::mdir::md_exec::JoinOp)

_Waits for the op that runs beside the ops before it_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.join` attr-dict
```

Belongs to the storage form. An op marked `md_exec.side` runs on a
second stream, beside the ops that follow it, up to the next
`md_exec.join` in its block: the ops that follow the join run after it.
Every op between the two must be independent of the marked op
(`md-exec-assign-streams`, D87).

```mlir
%e, %w = md_exec.reciprocal ... {md_exec.side}
md_exec.refresh_neighbors ...
md_exec.join
md_exec.particle_for ins(%forces, ...) ...
```

The op declares no effects, so that no pass moves an op across it, or
moves it.



### `md_exec.linear_transform` (::mdir::md_exec::LinearTransformOp)

_A linear transform with a declared adjoint_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.linear_transform` $input `outs` `(` $out `:` type($out) `)`
              `grid` `(` $grid `)` `kind` `(` $kind `)`
              `direction` `(` $direction `)` `adjoint` `(` $adjoint `)`
              `pairing` `(` $pairing `)` attr-dict `:` type($input)
```

Transforms a real grid of `grid[0] * grid[1] * grid[2]` values to or
from a packed Hermitian half-spectrum of
`2 * grid[0] * grid[1] * (grid[2] / 2 + 1)` real values. The complex
values are interleaved, with the last Fourier axis stored in half.
`forward` uses the negative exponent and `backward` the positive
exponent; neither divides by the number of grid points. Their
`adjoint` declares the opposite direction, and `pairing` declares
`real_hermitian_half`: the Euclidean real-grid inner product and the
real part of the complex product on the packed grid, with weight 1 at
last-axis frequency zero and the Nyquist frequency (when present),
and weight 2 at the other frequencies. The verifier checks both
declarations. The adjoint identity holds on the half-spectra of real
grids: the zero-frequency and, when present, Nyquist planes obey
Hermitian symmetry across the first two axes. An arbitrary packed
complex buffer is outside this contract. The backward transform may
overwrite its input, so users retain a copy
when its spectrum has another consumer.

The input and output are explicit buffers. A lowering may schedule
this transform after the data it reads and before consumers of its
output without synchronizing unrelated work. `fft3d` is the first
transform kind; later kinds use the same operation and adjoint rule.

```mlir
md_exec.linear_transform %real outs(%spectrum : memref<?xf64>)
  grid([8, 8, 8]) kind("fft3d") direction("forward")
  adjoint("backward") pairing("real_hermitian_half") : memref<?xf64>
```

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

### `md_exec.nonzero` (::mdir::md_exec::NonzeroOp)

_The places of the particles whose value is not zero_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.nonzero` $field (`outs` `(` $out^ `:` type($out) `)`)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($field)) (`->` qualified(type($result))^)?
```

Returns a field of `i32` whose first entries are the places of the
particles whose value in `field` is not zero, in ascending order, and
whose other entries are −1 − the place of each of the others, in
ascending order. A value that is not a number is not zero.
The reciprocal sum of PME spreads and gathers the particles of such a
list only (D262); where the particles are
put in a new order, the list is made again from the permuted field.

```mlir
%listed = md_exec.nonzero %q : !md.field<@atoms, f64>
            -> !md.field<@atoms, i32>
```

In the storage form the field is a buffer, and the list is written to
the buffer in `outs`, which holds one `i32` per particle. The entries
are counted in integers, so the list is the same in every mode.

```mlir
md_exec.nonzero %q outs(%listed : memref<?xi32>) : memref<?xf64>
```

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

| `field` | A per-particle field or buffer of a field |
| `out` | buffer of a field |

| Result | Description |

| `result` | A per-particle field |



### `md_exec.pair_for` (::mdir::md_exec::PairForOp)

_Runs a kernel over the pairs of a neighbor structure_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.pair_for` $neighbors `,` $positions `,` $cell (`centers` `(` $centers^ `)`)?
              (`center_set` `(` $centerSet^ `:` qualified(type($centerSet)) `)`)?
              (`ins` `(` $ins^ `:` qualified(type($ins)) `)`)?
              (`outs` `(` $outs^ `:` qualified(type($outs)) `)`)?
              (`reduce` `(` $reduce^ `:` type($reduce) `)`)?
              (`scratch` `(` $scratch^ `:` type($scratch) `)`)?
              `cutoff` `(` $cutoff `)`
              (`weights` $weights^)?
              (`overwrite` $overwrite^)?
              custom<ExchangeList>($exchange)
              (`images` `(` $images^ `)`)?
              `policy` `(` $traversal `,` $conflict `)`
              custom<Scatter>($scatter)
              $kernel attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($neighbors)) `,` qualified(type($positions))
              (`->` qualified(type($results))^)?
```

With the directed traversal, for every particle `i` and every entry `j`
of its list with `r_ij < cutoff`:

```text
a_i = a0_i + Σ_j k_a(i, j)          for every field in `outs`
S   = S0   + w · Σ_ij k_S(i, j)     for every value in `reduce`
```

The loop computes the displacement `d` and the squared distance `r2`
from the positions and the cell, and evaluates the cutoff predicate. The
kernel receives `r2`, `d`, and two values for each field in `ins`. It
yields one contribution for each field in `outs`, then one for each
value in `reduce`.

```mlir
%f, %u = md_exec.pair_for %nl, %x, %cell
           outs(%f0 : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>)
           reduce(%u0 : f64) cutoff(2.5) weights [0.5]
           policy(directed, owner_only) {
^bb0(%r2: f64, %d: vector<3xf64>):
  ...
  md_exec.yield %k_f, %k_u : vector<3xf64>, f64
} : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
    -> !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>, f64
```

In the storage form the positions and the fields are buffers. A buffer
in `outs` is updated where it is, and the op has results for the values
in `reduce` only. `overwrite` has one flag per buffer in `outs`: if it
is set, the loop ignores what the buffer holds, as if it held zeros. If
it is absent, no flag is set.

```mlir
%u = md_exec.pair_for %nl, %x, %cell
       outs(%f : memref<?x3xf64>) reduce(%u0 : f64)
       cutoff(2.5) weights [0.5] overwrite [true]
       policy(directed, owner_only) {
^bb0(%r2: f64, %d: vector<3xf64>):
  ...
  md_exec.yield %k_f, %k_u : vector<3xf64>, f64
} : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, memref<?x3xf64> -> f64
```

`scratch` holds buffers that the loop may use as it likes. What they
hold before and after is unspecified. On a device a loop needs two for
each value in `reduce`, of the type of a buffer with one value of the
type of the sum per particle: the first has a row a particle, the second
a row for each part of the reduction (`maxReductionParts`, #711).

`exchange` has one contract for each field in `outs` and then each
value in `reduce`, in the order of the yield: how the kernel of that
value behaves when the two particles are swapped, from the
`md.gather_relation` or `md.sum_relation` it came from. A loop may
compute a pair once for its two particles only if every value is
`symmetric` or `antisymmetric` (docs/neighbor-groups.md, D89). Without it,
every value is `none`.

```mlir
%f, %u = md_exec.pair_for %nl, %x, %cell
           outs(%f0 : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>)
           reduce(%u0 : f64) cutoff(2.5) weights [0.5]
           exchange [antisymmetric, symmetric]
           policy(directed, owner_only) { ... }
```

With `centers(%n)`, the loop takes the rows of the first `n` particles
only, the centers, whose entries are any particles of the set; it
updates a destination at the centers, and the other particles keep
what the destination holds. With `images(explicit)`, the displacement
is the plain difference `d = x_i − x_j` of the positions, which carry
their images, as the owned and ghost rows of a domain do, and no
minimum image is taken; the cell is still an operand. Both are those of
the structure (D290, docs/distributed-ml2.md, Section 7.2).

With the policy `(directed, atomic)`, every entry `(i, j)` of the list
adds `k_a(i, j)` at `i` and `σ k_a(i, j)` at `j`, where `σ` is +1 for
a `symmetric` destination and −1 for an `antisymmetric` one; the
additions at `j` are atomic. Every destination must be symmetric or
antisymmetric, and every sum symmetric. Over the owned and ghost rows
of a domain it is the two-ended `md_dist.gather_pairs`, whose
contributions at the ghosts return to their owners.

```mlir
%f = md_exec.pair_for %nl, %x, %cell centers(%n)
       outs(%f0 : !md.field<@dd.d0.local, 3 x f64>) cutoff(2.0)
       exchange [antisymmetric] images(explicit)
       policy(directed, atomic) { ... }
       : !mdrt.neighbors<@dd.d0.local>, !md.field<@dd.d0.local, 3 x f64>
       -> !md.field<@dd.d0.local, 3 x f64>
```

`scatter(hash(S, P, L))`, which `md-exec-choose-scatter` sets on a
device (D291, docs/device-primitives.md), states how a loop
whose conflict is `atomic` adds to the particles of a block's pairs:
through a table of `S` slots in block memory, at most `P` slots tried
before an atomic of the device, from `L` units of work of a launch on.
Without it, or with `scatter(atomic)`, by an atomic of the device for
each value. A loop takes no other strategy.

### `md_exec.particle_for` (::mdir::md_exec::ParticleForOp)

_Runs a kernel over particles_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.particle_for` (`ins` `(` $ins^ `:` qualified(type($ins)) `)`)?
              (`outs` `(` $outs^ `:` qualified(type($outs)) `)`)?
              (`reduce` `(` $reduce^ `:` type($reduce) `)`)?
              (`scratch` `(` $scratch^ `:` type($scratch) `)`)?
              $kernel attr-dict
              (`->` qualified(type($results))^)?
```

For every particle `i`:

```text
b_i = k_b(i)                 for every field in `outs`
S   = S0 + Σ_i k_S(i)        for every number or vector in `reduce`
A   = A0 or any_i k_A(i)     for every value of the type i1 in `reduce`
```

A field in `outs` is written, not accumulated into. Its old values are
not read.

A value of the type `i1` in `reduce` tells whether the kernel yields
true for any particle. It needs nothing in `scratch`: on a device, a
thread that yields true sets a flag, and the others do nothing.

The kernel receives one value for each field in `ins`. It yields one
value for each field in `outs`, then one contribution for each value in
`reduce`.

```mlir
%v1 = md_exec.particle_for
        ins(%v, %f, %m : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>,
                         !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>,
                         !md.field<@atoms, f64>)
        outs(%v0 : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>) {
^bb0(%v_i: vector<3xf64>, %f_i: vector<3xf64>, %m_i: f64):
  ...
  md_exec.yield %v_new : vector<3xf64>
} -> !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

In the storage form the fields are buffers. A buffer in `outs` is
written where it is, and the op has results for the values in `reduce`
only. A buffer may be in `ins` and in `outs`: the kernel of a particle
reads and writes the values of that particle only.

```mlir
md_exec.particle_for
    ins(%v, %f, %m : memref<?x3xf64>, memref<?x3xf64>, memref<?xf64>)
    outs(%v : memref<?x3xf64>) {
^bb0(%v_i: vector<3xf64>, %f_i: vector<3xf64>, %m_i: f64):
  ...
  md_exec.yield %v_new : vector<3xf64>
}
```

`scratch` is as for `md_exec.pair_for`.

```
operation ::= `md_exec.permute` $field `,` $order (`outs` `(` $out^ `:` type($out) `)`)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($field)) `,` qualified(type($order))
              (`->` qualified(type($result))^)?
```

the field.

```mlir

    : memref<?x3xf64>, memref<?xi32>
```

### `md_exec.radial` (::mdir::md_exec::RadialOp)

_A function of the squared distance alone_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.radial` $function `(` $r2 `)` attr-dict `:` type($r2) `->` type($result)
```

The value of the function `function`, of type `(f64) -> f64`, at the
squared distance `r2`: a part of a pair kernel that depends on the
distance only, such as the screened Coulomb force of Ewald summation
without its charges, which `md-exec-simplify-distance` separates under
`fast_math`. `md-exec-expand-radial` makes it a table of the function
in a kernel that computes in f32 (D94), and the function itself in one
that computes in f64.

```mlir
%g = md_exec.radial @md_radial_0(%r2) : f32
```

### `md_exec.reciprocal` (::mdir::md_exec::ReciprocalOp)

_The reciprocal sum of particle mesh Ewald_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.reciprocal` $positions `,` $charges `,` $cell `,` $moduli
              (`outs` `(` $out^ `:` type($out) `)`)?
              (`scratch` `(` $scratch^ `:` type($scratch) `)`)?
              `grid` `(` $grid `)` `order` `(` $order `)` `beta` `(` $beta `)`
              `coulomb` `(` $coulomb `)` (`dispersion` $dispersion^)?
              (`potential` $potential^)?
              (`prolate` $prolate^)?
              (`p3m` $p3m^)?
              (`listed` `(` $listed^ `:` qualified(type($listed)) `)`)?
              (`gather_all` $gather_all^)?
              custom<Scatter>($scatter)
              attr-dict `:` qualified(type($positions)) `,` qualified(type($charges))
              `,` qualified(type($moduli)) `->` type($energy) `,` type($virial)
              (`,` qualified(type($forces))^)?
```

What `md.reciprocal` computes: the energy, the virial, and the forces
of the reciprocal sum of smooth particle mesh Ewald (docs/pme.md).

```mlir
%u, %w, %f = md_exec.reciprocal %x, %q, %cell, %moduli
               grid([32, 32, 32]) order(4) beta(3.12) coulomb(138.935)
               : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>, !md.field<@atoms, f64>,
                 !md.table<2, f64>
               -> f64, vector<9xf64>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

In the storage form the fields and the table are buffers, the forces
are written to the buffer in `outs`, and `scratch` holds the grid: the
charges in fixed point, the grid in f64, and the half-complex grid of
its transform, then on a device the sums of the rows of the grid. The
op writes each buffer of `scratch` before it reads it, and what they
hold after it is unspecified, except the bricks of the spreading
(D108), which it finds zero and leaves zero; so the sums of a function
share the buffers of the same shape (D315). The op
reads and writes its scratch, so two sums that share a buffer are not
independent.

With `potential`, the field that the op yields is not the forces but
the derivative of the energy in the charge of each particle, one
number for each, the potential of the grid gathered with the weights
of the B-splines (the fourth result of `md.reciprocal`,
D231); the grid is computed in the type that this
field is stored in.

```mlir
%u, %w, %p = md_exec.reciprocal %x, %q, %cell, %moduli
               grid([32, 32, 32]) order(4) beta(3.12) coulomb(138.935)
               potential
               : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>, !md.field<@atoms, f64>,
                 !md.table<2, f64>
               -> f64, vector<9xf64>, !md.field<@atoms, f64>
```

With `p3m` (that of `md.reciprocal`, D304), the influence
function is eq. 2.28 of [Ballenegger2012], from the rows of `moduli`
that `md.reciprocal` describes; the factors of the edges take five
values a point instead of three.

With `listed`, the field of the places of the particles whose charge
can be nonzero that `md.reciprocal` takes (`md_exec.nonzero`,
D262), the spreading and the gathering
take those particles only, and the others take a force of zero. A sum
with `potential` takes no list. With `gather_all` (that of
`md.reciprocal`), a device gathers every particle, as without a list.

With `scatter(tile(E))`, which `md-exec-choose-scatter` sets on a
device (D285, docs/device-primitives.md), the charges
are spread through tiles of the memory of a block, one for each bin of
$E^3$ points of the grid, into which the particles are binned by their
first point at each evaluation (D282); without it, or with
`scatter(atomic)`, as before (into the bricks of D108 for splines of
order 4 in f32, by atomics of the device into the grid otherwise). The
deterministic mode takes no tiles: its grid is in fixed point (D70,
D84). A sum takes no other strategy.

```mlir
%u, %w, %f = md_exec.reciprocal %x, %q, %cell, %moduli
               grid([64, 64, 64]) order(4) beta(3.12) coulomb(138.935)
               scatter(tile(8))
               : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f32>, !md.field<@atoms, f32>,
                 !md.table<2, f32>
               -> f64, vector<9xf64>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f32>
```

### `md_exec.reference_cell` (::mdir::md_exec::ReferenceCellOp)

_The cell that a neighbor structure was built in_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.reference_cell` $neighbors (`pruned` $pruned^)? attr-dict `:` qualified(type($neighbors))
```

Returns the cell that `neighbors` was built in. For a structure that
has not been built, it is unspecified. With the cell of the step, it
tells how far a barostat has scaled the configuration since the build,
which the test of validity allows for (D80).

```mlir
%cell0 = md_exec.reference_cell %nl : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>
```

With `pruned`, the cell in which the inner list of a dual list was last
pruned (D114).

### `md_exec.reference_positions` (::mdir::md_exec::ReferencePositionsOp)

_The configuration that a neighbor structure was built at_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.reference_positions` $neighbors (`pruned` $pruned^)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($neighbors)) `->` qualified(type($result))
```

Returns the positions `x_ref` that `neighbors` was built at. For a
structure that has not been built, the values are unspecified.

```mlir
%ref = md_exec.reference_positions %nl
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms> -> !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

A loop over particles tests with them whether the structure is still
valid, and hands the result to `md_exec.refresh_neighbors` as `moved`:

```mlir
%moved = md_exec.particle_for ins(%x, %ref : ...) reduce(%false : i1) {
^bb0(%x_i: vector<3xf64>, %ref_i: vector<3xf64>):
  ...   // |x_i − ref_i|² > (skin / 2)²
  md_exec.yield %far : i1
} -> i1
```

Such a loop can be fused with the loop that writes the positions. The
test then costs no loop of its own.

In the storage form the result is the buffer of the structure that
holds the positions. A refresh that builds the structure writes to it.

```mlir
%ref = md_exec.reference_positions %nl
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms> -> memref<?x3xf64>
```

With `pruned`, the positions at which the inner list of a dual list
was last pruned (D114).

### `md_exec.refresh_neighbors` (::mdir::md_exec::RefreshNeighborsOp)

_A neighbor structure that is valid for a configuration_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.refresh_neighbors` $neighbors `,` $positions `,` $cell
              (`scratch` `(` $scratch^ `:` type($scratch) `)`)?
              (`moved` `(` $moved^ `)`)? (`stale` `(` $stale^ `)`)?
              (`centers` `(` $centers^ `)`)?
              `cutoff` `(` $cutoff `)` `skin` `(` $skin `)`
              (`prune_skin` `(` $prune_skin^ `)`)?
              `cell_width` `(` $cell_width `)` (`interval` `(` $interval^ `)`)?
              (`images` `(` $images^ `)`)?
              `policy` `(` $policy `)` attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($neighbors)) `,` qualified(type($positions))
```

Returns `neighbors` if it is valid for the configuration `positions` in
the cell `cell`, and a structure built at that configuration otherwise.

A structure that was built at the configuration `x_ref` in the cell of
edges `L_ref` is valid in the cell of edges `L` when, with the scale
`m = L / L_ref` of each axis, `R = cutoff + skin`, and `r_c = cutoff`,

```text
2 max_i |x_i − m ⊙ x_ref,i| ≤ min(m) R − r_c
```

Under that condition it contains every pair within the cutoff: a pair
that it leaves out was farther than `R` apart at the build, so it is
farther than `min(m) R − 2 max_i |x_i − m ⊙ x_ref,i|` apart now. In
the cell of the build the condition is `max_i |x_i − x_ref,i| ≤ skin /
2`; a barostat that scales the positions with the cell costs only the
margin `(1 − min(m)) R` (D80). With the
policy `always` the structure is built whether it is valid or not.

`cell_width` is the least width of the cells that a rebuild bins the
particles into. The build chooses the width from the density of the
particles: the cutoff plus the skin, half of it, or a third.

```mlir
%nl1 = md_exec.refresh_neighbors %nl, %x, %cell
         cutoff(2.5) skin(0.3) cell_width(2.8) policy(check)
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

In the storage form `positions` is a buffer. The structure is rebuilt
where it is, and the result is `neighbors` itself.

```mlir
%nl1 = md_exec.refresh_neighbors %nl, %x, %cell
         cutoff(2.5) skin(0.3) cell_width(2.8) policy(check)
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, memref<?x3xf64>
```

With the policy `interval`, the structure is built at the first
refresh and at every `interval`-th refresh since the last build,
whether it is valid or not; the displacements are tested only at those
refreshes, before the build, and a build that finds the structure no
longer valid is counted (`mdrtCountLateBuild`): pairs within the cutoff
may have been missed since. The test does not see a particle that went
too far and came back within the interval. Not a default of any run
(`md-exec-rebuild-at-interval`, D88).

```mlir
%nl1 = md_exec.refresh_neighbors %nl, %x, %cell
         cutoff(2.5) skin(0.3) cell_width(2.8) interval(10)
         policy(interval)
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

`scratch` holds buffers that the op may use as it likes. What they hold
before and after is unspecified. On a device the test of validity needs
two, of the type of a buffer with one value of the type of the positions
per particle: the first has a row a particle, the second a row for each
part of the reduction (`maxReductionParts`, #711).

With `moved`, the op does not test the displacements: `moved` tells
whether the condition above fails for a particle. A loop over particles
computes it from the positions, `md_exec.reference_positions`, and the
cells (`md_exec.reference_cell`). The op then needs nothing in
`scratch`.

```mlir
%nl1 = md_exec.refresh_neighbors %nl, %x, %cell moved(%moved)
         cutoff(2.5) skin(0.3) cell_width(2.8) policy(check)
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

With `prune_skin` the structure is a dual list (D114,
docs/neighbor-tiles.md, Section 6): the outer list, built with the reach
`R = cutoff + skin` as above, and an inner one pruned from it, which
keeps the pairs of the outer list within `R_in = cutoff + prune_skin`
at the configuration `x_p` and the cell `L_p` of the pruning; the
loops over pairs take the inner one. With `m_p = L / L_p`, the inner
list holds every pair within the cutoff while the outer one is valid
and

```text
2 max_i |x_i − m_p ⊙ x_p,i| ≤ min(m_p) R_in − r_c
```

`stale` tells whether this condition fails for a particle; the loop
that computes it takes `md_exec.reference_positions` and
`md_exec.reference_cell` with `pruned`. Where the outer list is not
valid the op builds it and prunes the inner one from it; where only
`stale` is set it prunes again, which reads the outer list and the
positions and searches nothing. A pair dropped by one pruning may come
back, so the inner list is always pruned from the outer one.

```mlir
%nl1 = md_exec.refresh_neighbors %nl, %x, %cell moved(%moved)
         stale(%stale) cutoff(2.5) skin(0.6) prune_skin(0.2)
         cell_width(2.8) policy(check)
         : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

`centers` and `images` are as for `md_exec.build_neighbors`. A
structure with either is refreshed with the policy `always` only and is
not a dual list: the test of validity over explicit images belongs to
the migration of particles between domains (docs/distributed-ml2.md,
Section 8).

Traits: `AttrSizedOperandSegments`

### `md_exec.renumber` (::mdir::md_exec::RenumberOp)

_The members of tuples in the current order of the particles_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.renumber` $members `,` $ids attr-dict `:` qualified(type($members)) `,`
              qualified(type($ids))
```

The members of the tuples of a topology are places of particles. Where
the particles are put in another order, their places change. This op
takes the members as they are in the order of the files, and the
numbers of the particles in the current order, `ids`, which say for
each place the particle of the files that is there, and returns the
members at their current places.

```text
member' = the place p with ids[p] = member
```

```mlir
%angles1 = md_exec.renumber %angles, %ids
    : !md.relation<@atoms, 3, reversal, @angles>, !md.field<@atoms, i32>
```

In the storage form the op takes buffers and returns a new buffer of
the host, which lasts to the end of the block that it is in.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `members` | A set of tuples of distinct particles or buffer of the members of tuples |
| `ids` | A per-particle field or buffer of a field |

#### Results:

| Result | Description |
| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | A set of tuples of distinct particles or buffer of the members of tuples |



### `md_exec.reset_neighbors` (::mdir::md_exec::ResetNeighborsOp)

_Makes a neighbor structure valid for no configuration_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.reset_neighbors` $neighbors (`exclude` `(` $excluded^ `:` type($excluded) `)`)? attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($neighbors))
```

Belongs to the storage form. The storage of a structure is allocated in
the body of the function. Where the value form has an empty structure
inside a loop, the storage form resets the structure, so that every
iteration begins with a structure that the first refresh builds. On a
device a structure may take the storage of an earlier one of the same
shape that nothing uses any more, such as the structure of the
evaluation at the start for that of the steps; it is reset where it
begins (D330).

The count of builds starts again from zero.

```mlir
md_exec.reset_neighbors %nl : !mdrt.neighbors<@atoms>
```

With `exclude`, the builds from here on leave out the pairs of that
incidence structure, in place of those that the structure had. A loop
whose iterations renumber the particles gives each iteration its own.

#### Operands:

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `neighbors` | A physical neighbor structure |
| `excluded` | buffer of the tuples of each particle |



### `md_exec.scatter_add` (::mdir::md_exec::ScatterAddOp)

_Adds values into a field at the rows that indices name_

For every row `k` of `values` and `indices` (D291,
docs/device-primitives.md):

```text
a'_i = a_i + Σ_{k : idx_k = i} v_k
```

`values` and `indices` are fields of one set, the indices of `i32`;
`dest` is a field of the set that the indices name rows of, with the
components and the type of the values. An index must be a row of the
destination; the op does not check it.

```mlir
%a1 = md_exec.scatter_add %v at %idx into %a0
        : !md.field<@ghosts, 3 x f64>, !md.field<@ghosts, i32>
          -> !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
```

In the storage form the op takes buffers and updates the destination
where it is; it has no result. `overwrite(true)` means that it ignores
what the destination holds, as if it held zeros.

```mlir
md_exec.scatter_add %v at %idx into %a overwrite(false)
    : memref<?x3xf64, 1>, memref<?xi32, 1>, memref<?x3xf64, 1>
```

`scatter(hash(S, P, L))`, which `md-exec-choose-scatter` sets on a
device, states that the values of a block are added in a table of `S`
slots in block memory first, at most `P` slots tried before an atomic of
the device, from `L` values on. Without it, or with `scatter(atomic)`,
an atomic of the device for each value. `tile` and `sorted` are refused.

Interfaces: `LoopEffectOpInterface`, `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

<tr><td><code>scatter</code></td><td>::mdir::md_exec::ScatterAttr</td><td>The strategy of a scatter-accumulate</td></tr>
</table>

### `md_exec.spatial_order` (::mdir::md_exec::SpatialOrderOp)

_Computes the order of the particles by cell_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.spatial_order` $positions `,` $cell `,` $ids
              (`outs` `(` $order^ `:` type($order) `)`)?
              `width` `(` $width `)` attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($positions)) `,` qualified(type($ids))
              (`->` qualified(type($result))^)?
```

Returns the order in which the particles follow one another in space:
by the cell that they are in, in cells that are `width` wide or wider,
and within a cell by `ids`. Entry `k` of the order is the particle that
comes to place `k`.

The cells are numbered along x first, then along y and z. Particles
that are near one another in space are then near one another in
memory, and a loop over pairs reads the neighbors of a particle from
few places.

`ids` holds a number for each particle that no other particle has. The
order depends on the positions and on these numbers only, not on the
order that the particles are in. A run that continues from a
checkpoint therefore arrives at the order of the run that was not
interrupted.

```mlir
%order = md_exec.spatial_order %x, %cell, %ids width(1.4)
           : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>, !md.field<@atoms, i32>
           -> !mdrt.permutation<@atoms>
```

In the storage form the fields are buffers, and the order is written
to the buffer in `outs`, which holds one `i32` per particle.

```mlir
md_exec.spatial_order %x, %cell, %ids outs(%order : memref<?xi32>)
    width(1.4) : memref<?x3xf64>, memref<?xi32>
```

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface`

<tr><td><code>width</code></td><td>::mlir::FloatAttr</td><td>64-bit float attribute</td></tr>
</table>

| :-----: | ----------- |
| `positions` | A per-particle field or buffer of a field |
| `cell` | A simulation cell |
| `ids` | A per-particle field or buffer of a field |
| `order` | buffer of a field |

#### Results:

| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | An order of the particles of a set |



### `md_exec.tabulate` (::mdir::md_exec::TabulateOp)

_A table computed entry by entry from other tables_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.tabulate` `(` $tables `:` qualified(type($tables)) `)` $kernel attr-dict
              `->` qualified(type($result))
```

For every entry of the tables, which all have one rank and the same
number of types, the kernel takes the value of each table there and
yields the value of the new table. A kernel whose values depend on the
types of a pair through tables only computes them once per pair of
types this way (`md-exec-fold-tables`), not once per pair of
particles. The kernel computes in f64; the new table is symmetric if
every table it comes from is.

```mlir
%a = md_exec.tabulate (%sigma, %epsilon : !md.table<2, f64, symmetric>,
                                          !md.table<2, f64, symmetric>) {
^bb0(%s: f64, %e: f64):
  %s2 = arith.mulf %s, %s : f64
  ...
  md_exec.yield %a : f64
} -> !md.table<2, f64, symmetric>
```

`md-exec-assign-storage` computes the table on the host, where the
tables it comes from are, and puts it where the loops that read it are.

Traits: `AlwaysSpeculatableImplTrait`, `SingleBlock`

Interfaces: `ConditionallySpeculatable`, `NoMemoryEffect (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

| Operand | Description |
| :-----: | ----------- |
| `tables` | variadic of A table of parameters, indexed by types |

#### Results:

| Result | Description |
| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | A table of parameters, indexed by types |



### `md_exec.tuple_for` (::mdir::md_exec::TupleForOp)

_Runs a kernel over the tuples of each particle_

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `md_exec.tuple_for` $incidence `,` $positions `,` $cell
              custom<Coordinates>($coordinate_kinds, $coordinate_members)
              (`ins` `(` $ins^ `:` qualified(type($ins)) `)`)?
              (`tuple` `(` $parameters^ `:` qualified(type($parameters)) `)`)?
              (`outs` `(` $outs^ `:` qualified(type($outs)) `)`)?
              (`reduce` `(` $reduce^ `:` type($reduce) `)`)?
              (`scratch` `(` $scratch^ `:` type($scratch) `)`)?
              `arity` `(` $arity `)`
              (`overwrite` $overwrite^)?
              (`disjoint` $disjoint^)?
              custom<Scatter>($scatter)
              $kernel attr-dict
              `:` qualified(type($incidence)) `,` qualified(type($positions))
              (`->` qualified(type($results))^)?
```

For every particle `i` and every tuple `t` that it is a member of, at
the place `s`:

```text
a_i = a0_i + Σ_t k_a(t)[s]          for every field in `outs`
S   = S0   + Σ_{t : s = 0} k_S(t)   for every number or vector in `reduce`
A   = A0 or any_t k_A(t)            for every value of the type i1 in `reduce`
```

A tuple of `k` members is evaluated `k` times, once by each of its
members, and every member takes its own part. A sum takes the
contribution of a tuple from the member at place 0, so that a tuple
counts once.

A value of the type `i1` in `reduce` tells whether the kernel yields
true for any tuple, as in `md_exec.particle_for`. It needs nothing in
`scratch`: on a device, a thread that yields true sets a flag of the
loop's own, and the others do nothing.

The loop computes the displacements that `coordinates` names, each in
the minimum image, from the positions and the cell. The kernel receives
them, then one value for each member for each field in `ins`, then one
value for each field in `tuple`. It yields one value for each member
for each field in `outs`, then one contribution for each value in
`reduce`.

```mlir
%f, %u = md_exec.tuple_for %incidence, %x, %cell
           coordinates(displacement(0, 1), displacement(2, 1))
           tuple(%k : !md.field<@angles, f64>)
           outs(%f0 : !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>) reduce(%u0 : f64)
           arity(3) {
^bb0(%u: vector<3xf64>, %v: vector<3xf64>, %k_t: f64):
  ...
  md_exec.yield %f_0, %f_1, %f_2, %e
      : vector<3xf64>, vector<3xf64>, vector<3xf64>, f64
} : !mdrt.incidence<@atoms, 3, @angles>, !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>
    -> !md.field<@atoms, 3 x f64>, f64
```

The storage form is as that of `md_exec.pair_for`, with `overwrite` and
`scratch`.

`disjoint` states that no particle is a member of two tuples, as the
tuple set declares (`md.tuple_set`). The results are the same; a
lowering may evaluate each tuple once, by its member at place 0, and
write to all of its members.

`scatter(hash(S, P, L))`, which `md-exec-choose-scatter` sets on a
device (D285, docs/device-primitives.md), states how a
lowering that evaluates each tuple once adds to the members: through a
table of `S` slots of the particles of a block in block memory, at
most `P` slots tried before an atomic of the device, from `L` tuples of
a launch on (D283). Without it, or with `scatter(atomic)`, by an atomic
of the device for each value. A loop takes no other strategy.

Traits: `AttrSizedOperandSegments`, `RecursiveMemoryEffects`, `SingleBlock`

## Attributes

### AlgebraListAttr

_The algebra of each value that an op reduces_

One algebra for each value that an op reduces, in the order of
`md_exec::algebra::getReducedTypes` (D301,
include/mdir/Dialect/MDExec/Algebra.h): a loop's destinations, then its
`reduce`; the destination of `md_exec.scatter_add`; the spreading, the
energy, and the virial of `md_exec.reciprocal`; the sum of
`md_dist.all_reduce` and of `md_dist.halo_sum`.

Each is a licence to the lowering about the order of evaluation
(ruled on #470):

- `any_order_exact`: the lowering may evaluate in any order and
  grouping, and every order gives the same bits (integers, `or`, fixed
  point).
- `any_order`: the lowering may evaluate in any order and grouping. For
  floating-point values the result's rounding then depends on that
  order. This is the floating-point sums of the default mode.
- `fixed_order`: the lowering must use the order the IR states, or an
  exact form of the sum, so that the result is the same on every run of
  the same build. For `md_dist` this holds for a given decomposition
  (#409).

`fixed_order` may be met through an `any_order_exact` form: the
fixed-point spreading of PME in the deterministic mode is the case.

The licence is about order only. `any_order` permits any order and
grouping; it does not permit changing the accumulator's precision (an
f64 sum taken in f32) or the order of growth of its rounding error (a
tree replaced by a serial chain of atomics). Such a change is a
separate decision, with its own measurement.

`md-exec-assign-algebra` states it as `md_exec.algebra`, a discardable
attribute: a pass that rebuilds the op without it loses the fact, and
the lowerings then refuse the op rather than assume an algebra.

```mlir
{md_exec.algebra = #md_exec.algebra<any_order, any_order_exact>}
```

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| values | `::llvm::ArrayRef<::mdir::md_exec::Algebra>` |  |

### ScatterAttr

_The strategy of a scatter-accumulate_

How an op adds values into a field at indices that its threads share
(D285, docs/device-primitives.md):

| Form | Strategy |
|---|---|
| `atomic` | an atomic addition of the device for each value |
| `tile(E)` | a dense tile in block memory for each bin of $E^3$ points |
| `hash(S, P, L)` | a hash table of `S` slots in block memory, at most `P` slots tried before a direct atomic, taken from `L` items on |
| `sorted` | reserved for #417 |

`md-exec-choose-scatter` sets it where the strategy's preconditions
hold (include/mdir/Dialect/MDExec/Scatter.h); the lowering checks them
with the same functions.

```mlir
#md_exec.scatter<tile(8)>
#md_exec.scatter<hash(512, 8, 100000)>
```

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| strategy | `::mdir::md_exec::ScatterStrategy` |  |
| edge | `int64_t` |  |
| slots | `int64_t` |  |
| probes | `int64_t` |  |
| least | `int64_t` |  |
